messages.author: 11316400dcae08ba
messages.subject: subread/exactSNP in cancer DNA-seq
parts:
Hello all,

I'm relatively new to bioinformatics, so apologies for a few, possibly obvious, questions!

1. Does anyone know if there are any comparative studies looking at the sensitivity/specificity of ExactSNP versus other callers (eg mutect or platypus), particularly in the context of sequencing cancer?

2. Is there any theoretical reason that ExactSNP might be better or worse at DNA NGS in cancer?  I ask because the bioinformaticians I've met at my institute tend to use BWA for read alignment in cancer DNA-seq, and I see the paper (Liao Y, Smyth GK and Shi W (2013). ExactSNP: an efficient and accurate SNP calling algorithm. In preparation) is still in preparation - I'm guessing it would contain some comparisons when published.  I understand other methods of calling variants use HMM, which can try to factor in some structual variation (haploid/3/4-ploid etc) when attempting to call variants - I just wonder how exactSNP signal vs noise works for this.

3. Is there any necessity / advantage to sorting the resulting BAM file prior to running exactSNP?

Many thanks in advance for your help.

All best,
Duncan.

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: subread/exactSNP in cancer DNA-seq
parts:
The ExactSNP work hasn't been published yet (delayed due to other projects). We hope to publish it soon.

You do not need to sort the bam file before feeding it to exactSNP.

Best wishes,

Wei
